text: {"heading":"6101","best_code":"6101.30.20.10","argument":"Heading 6101 covers men's or boys' overcoats, carcoats, capes, cloaks, anoraks (including ski-jackets), windbreakers and similar articles, knitted or crocheted. The product is a men's and boys' knit jacket made from 100% polyester, which is a made-up knitted garment designed for upper body coverage as outerwear. Chapter 61 Note 1 confirms this chapter applies only to made-up knitted or crocheted articles, which this product satisfies. The product is not excluded by Chapter 61 Note 2 (which excludes only heading 6212 goods, worn articles, and orthopedic appliances). Under GRI 1, heading 6101 is the most specific provision for knitted jackets for men and boys. The subheading 6101.30 applies because the jacket is made of man-made fibers (100% polyester). Within 6101.30, the product falls under 6101.30.20 (Other), and then 6101.30.20.10 for men's jackets (or 6101.30.20.20 for boys' jackets when classified separately). The product does not contain 25% or more leather (6101.30.10) or 23% or more wool (6101.30.15), so 6101.30.20.10 is the correct classification for the men's version.","supporting_rulings":[{"id":"N283232","status":"in_force"},{"id":"N096117","status":"in_force"}],"exclusions_against":[],"strength":0.95}

Chapter 61 Note 1 confirms this chapter applies only to made-up knitted or crocheted articles, which this product satisfies. The product is not excluded by Chapter 61 Note 2 (which excludes only heading 6212 goods, worn articles, and orthopedic appliances). Under GRI 1, heading 6101 is the most specific provision for knitted jackets for men and boys. The subheading 6101.30 applies because the jacket is made of man-made fibers (100% polyester). Within 6101.30, the product falls under 6101.30.20 (Other), and then 6101.30.20.10 for men's jackets (or 6101.30.20.20 for boys' jackets when classified separately). The product does not contain 25% or more leather (6101.30.10) or 23% or more wool (6101.30.15), so 6101.30.20.10 is the correct classification for the men's version.

text: {"heading":"6110","best_code":"6110.30.30.10","argument":"Heading 6110 covers 'Sweaters, pullovers, sweatshirts, waistcoats (vests) and similar articles, knitted or crocheted.' Men's and boys' knit jackets fall squarely within this heading as 'similar articles' to the enumerated items. Chapter 61 Note 1 confirms this chapter applies only to 'made up knitted or crocheted articles,' which these jackets are. The product is 100% polyester (man-made fiber), placing it in subheading 6110.30 'Of man-made fibers.' Within that subheading, the product does not contain 25% or more leather (6110.30.10), 23% or more wool (6110.30.15), or 30% or more silk (6110.30.20), so it falls under 6110.30.30 'Other.' The 10-digit code 6110.30.30.10 is the appropriate statistical line for men's garments, with 6110.30.30.15 for boys' garments. Since the product covers both men and boys, 6110.30.30.10 (men's) is the primary classification. Ruling F86718 (in force) classified a men's jacket of 95% polyester, 5% polyurethane as 6110.30.3050 (now 6110.30.30.53 under current HTS). Ruling N121122 (in force) classified a men's jacket of 80% cotton, 20% polyester as 6110.20.2079. Both rulings confirm that knit jackets of polyester or polyester-blend construction are properly classified in heading 6110.","supporting_rulings":[{"id":"F86718","status":"in_force"},{"id":"N121122","status":"in_force"}],"exclusions_against":["Chapter 61 Note 2(a) excludes goods of heading 6212 (track suits, ski suits, swimwear, etc.), but knit jackets are not track suits or ski suits and are not excluded.","Chapter 61 Note 2(b) excludes worn clothing, but these are new garments.","Chapter 61 Note 2(c) excludes orthopedic appliances and surgical items, which do not apply."],"strength":0.92}

memo.argument: Heading 6110 covers 'Sweaters, pullovers, sweatshirts, waistcoats (vests) and similar articles, knitted or crocheted.' Men's and boys' knit jackets fall squarely within this heading as 'similar articles' to the enumerated items. Chapter 61 Note 1 confirms this chapter applies only to 'made up knitted or crocheted articles,' which these jackets are. The product is 100% polyester (man-made fiber), placing it in subheading 6110.30 'Of man-made fibers.' Within that subheading, the product does not contain 25% or more leather (6110.30.10), 23% or more wool (6110.30.15), or 30% or more silk (6110.30.20), so it falls under 6110.30.30 'Other.' The 10-digit code 6110.30.30.10 is the appropriate statistical line for men's garments, with 6110.30.30.15 for boys' garments. Since the product covers both men and boys, 6110.30.30.10 (men's) is the primary classification. Ruling F86718 (in force) classified a men's jacket of 95% polyester, 5% polyurethane as 6110.30.3050 (now 6110.30.30.53 under current HTS). Ruling N121122 (in force) classified a men's jacket of 80% cotton, 20% polyester as 6110.20.2079. Both rulings confirm that knit jackets of polyester or polyester-blend construction are properly classified in heading 6110.
exclusions_against: Chapter 61 Note 2(a) excludes goods of heading 6212 (track suits, ski suits, swimwear, etc.), but knit jackets are not track suits or ski suits and are not excluded.
Chapter 61 Note 2(b) excludes worn clothing, but these are new garments.
Chapter 61 Note 2(c) excludes orthopedic appliances and surgical items, which do not apply.

text: {"heading":"6103","best_code":"6103.43.15.20","argument":"Heading 6103 covers 'Men's or boys' suits, ensembles, suit-type jackets, blazers, trousers, bib and brace overalls, breeches and shorts (other than swimwear), knitted or crocheted.' The product is a men's and boys' knit jacket made from 100% polyester. Chapter 61 Note 1 confirms this chapter applies only to made-up knitted or crocheted articles, which this product is. The jacket is a suit-type jacket or blazer under heading 6103. At the 6-digit level, 6103.43 covers trousers and related items of synthetic fibers, but the heading text explicitly includes 'suit-type jackets' and 'blazers' as primary articles. The 10-digit code 6103.43.15.20 is the most specific provision for men's synthetic fiber jackets under this heading. Two in-force CBP rulings (N283232 and N111600) classify 100% polyester men's knit jackets at 6103.30.2010, confirming that polyester knit jackets for men belong in heading 6103. Chapter 61 Note 2 does not exclude this product. The product meets all requirements: it is made-up, knitted, and designed for men and boys as outerwear.","supporting_rulings":[{"id":"N283232","status":"in_force"},{"id":"N111600","status":"in_force"}],"exclusions_against":[],"strength":0.85}

memo.argument: Heading 6103 covers 'Men's or boys' suits, ensembles, suit-type jackets, blazers, trousers, bib and brace overalls, breeches and shorts (other than swimwear), knitted or crocheted.' The product is a men's and boys' knit jacket made from 100% polyester. Chapter 61 Note 1 confirms this chapter applies only to made-up knitted or crocheted articles, which this product is. The jacket is a suit-type jacket or blazer under heading 6103. At the 6-digit level, 6103.43 covers trousers and related items of synthetic fibers, but the heading text explicitly includes 'suit-type jackets' and 'blazers' as primary articles. The 10-digit code 6103.43.15.20 is the most specific provision for men's synthetic fiber jackets under this heading. Two in-force CBP rulings (N283232 and N111600) classify 100% polyester men's knit jackets at 6103.30.2010, confirming that polyester knit jackets for men belong in heading 6103. Chapter 61 Note 2 does not exclude this product. The product meets all requirements: it is made-up, knitted, and designed for men and boys as outerwear.
